explanation:
[EFFECT] Temperature has a strong, non-monotonic (inverted-U-shaped) effect on predicted bike demand. Very cold temperatures (roughly below 10°C, normalised temp < 0.25) push predicted demand sharply downward — contributions drop as low as –0.9 in log space. Demand rises steeply as temperatures warm up, peaking around 25–27°C (normalised ≈ 0.60–0.65) where the contribution reaches approximately +0.25 to +0.30 in log space — meaning the model predicts noticeably more rentals. Beyond this sweet spot, at very high temperatures (above ~35°C, normalised > 0.85), the contribution falls back toward zero or slightly negative, indicating that extreme heat also suppresses demand.

[IMPORTANCE] Temperature is the **3rd most important feature** out of nine, with a global importance score of 0.197 — essentially tied with year (0.200) and far ahead of month, humidity, and wind speed. Only the hour of day is clearly more impactful, making temperature a primary driver of demand after time-of-day.

[RECOMMENDATION] Operators should plan for significantly higher bike availability and staffing in mild-to-warm weather (roughly 20–28°C), while scaling back expectations — and potentially maintenance — during cold spells or extreme heat waves, as both significantly reduce predicted demand.
